messages:
tim: FYI — noticed a GitHub Actions run that printed a short-lived session token to the job logs this morning. likely from a step that echoes env vars.
sec-bot: alert triggered: GH_ACTIONS_LOG_CRED_EXPOSURE detected (run_id: 48392). severity: medium.
maria: can you paste the snippet or redacted lines? we need the exact token prefix to identify usage.
tim: redacted: `***EXp-abc123` (last 6 chars shown). step name: `deploy:fetch-secrets`.
alex: do we know what that token was scoped to? GH OIDC? AWS_SESSION? service account?
jamal: looks like an AWS session token created via OIDC in the workflow. it had `sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` role arn: `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ci-deploy-role`.
sasha: pull audit logs from AWS for STS events around 2026-03-20 08:10 UTC. check CloudTrail for `AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` with that role and subject.
linda: I'll run a query now — running: `aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity --start-time 2026-03-20T08:00:00Z --end-time 2026-03-20T08:30:00Z`
ops-bot: deploy-job-48392 finished; logs archived to s3://redwood-ci-logs/2026/03/20/48392.log (access limited).
sec-bot: note: token was short-lived (1h). still treat as exposed until proven unused. recommended actions: (1) identify any API calls made with that session, (2) rotate any credentials that could be minted from that role if misuse detected, (3) redact CI logs and patch workflow to stop emitting env.
maria: jamal/linda — any signs of suspicious API calls from that assumed role?
jamal: initial CloudTrail scan shows normal deploy API calls (Describe*, GetObject, PutObject) from the role between 08:11-08:16 UTC. no console login or IAM changes observed.
linda: no signs of access from unfamiliar IPs. most calls from AWS-managed EKS nodes (10.x.x.x).
ima?: (reaction) :thumbsup:
sec-bot: cross-check KMS usage: list KMS Decrypt/GenerateDataKey events for the role in the same window. if the role could have requested plaintext secrets, that's higher severity.
alex: good call — `kms:Decrypt` is allowed for the role on key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01`.
maria: if KMS Decrypt was used, we need to verify which customer-related secrets could be impacted. start by enumerating which secrets that role can access in Secrets Manager/Parameter Store.
jamal: running secrets manager filter: `aws secretsmanager list-secret-version-ids --secret-id <secret>` is slow; I'll query IAM policy and resource ARNs.
sasha: quick wins: (a) invalidate any session tokens we can (AWS sessions can't be explicitly revoked) so rotate underlying long-lived creds, (b) rotate service credentials that can be used to assume that role (OIDC trust and role config), (c) remove `kms:Decrypt` until we confirm necessity.
linda: note — AWS sessions issued via STS can't be revoked, true. but we can change the role's trust policy to temporarily block GitHub OIDC issuer or add conditions so tokens minted after a cutoff are rejected.
maria: timeline + comms: we should treat as incident: contain -> assess -> notify. Containment: patch GitHub workflow to stop echoing env and remove printing, redact archived logs, and tighten role trust.
sec-bot: recommended RBAC change: add condition `StringNotEquals` on `token.issueTime` or require `aws:RequestedRegion` tag, or temporarily add `Deny` for `kms:Decrypt` for the role.
alex: I'll open a quick PR to the workflow to `set -o pipefail` and remove `echo $AWS_SESSION_TOKEN`. also add `::add-mask::${{ secrets.AWS_SESSION_TOKEN }}` for GH masking.
jamal: I'll create an IAM policy change to restrict `kms:Decrypt` for that role and add a condition to only allow from our CI OIDC provider with specific `sub` claim.
sasha: inventory of potential customer impact: which customers' data could be touched by the APIs called? check S3 bucket access logs and object prefixes used in the deploy step.
linda: preliminary S3 check: deploy writes to `customers/preview/*` and `models/shared/*`. no writes to `customer-prod/` prefixes observed.
maria: create a CS + legal notification draft in case we need to escalate. but we might be able to avoid customer notification if no customer data was accessed. keep decision internal until EOD.
sec-bot: post-incident actions (suggested): 1) Add log redaction in GH Action runner (prevent env prints). 2) Force rotation of any long-lived creds that can mint the role. 3) Add a CI-only KMS key and remove decryption permissions from cross-prod roles. 4) Add automated detection rule for tokens printed to logs. 5) Backfill CloudTrail/Stackdriver audit parse for last 7 days to ensure no prior exposures.
ops-bot: ticket created: SEC-INC-2026-042, linked to playbook: github-actions-credentials-exposure.
alex: quick question on KMS integration — can we rotate the KMS key without decrypting existing ciphertext used in deploy artifacts? any constraints?
jamal: rotating a symmetric CMK rotates the key material; AWS supports automatic rotation for customer-managed keys, but existing ciphertext must be re-encrypted if we require different key policies. we can create a new key and update secrets to use it. that's safer.
sasha: timeline: containment steps done or in progress: patch workflow (PR 1942) merged, logs redaction requested (s3 lifecycle), trust policy locked down (temp deny for oidc sub wildcard). still: scan for any API calls after 09:00 UTC.
linda: will run full CloudTrail extraction, will update ticket.
maria: action owners: alex (workflow fix + masking), jamal (IAM/KMS changes), linda (audit + S3 verification), sasha (customer impact + comms), tim (initial detection + follow-ups).
sec-bot: note to postmortem: add CI runner hardening item and implement KMS least-privilege guide for CI roles.
maria: thanks all. keep updates in thread. I'll draft internal comms once audit results are in.
sec-bot: incident severity set to MED until audit completes.
ops-bot: next status check scheduled at 2026-03-20T12:00:00Z.
